name: BICEP / Keck XIII: Improved Constraints on Primordial Gravitational Waves using Planck, WMAP, and BICEP/Keck Observations through the 2018 Observing Season
notes: Published in Phys. Rev. Lett. 127, 151301 (2021) per the official BICEP/Keck publication list.

official_url.quote: BICEP / Keck XIII: Improved Constraints on Primordial Gravitational Waves using Planck, WMAP, and BICEP/Keck Observations through the 2018 Observing Season

summary.plain: Combining every BICEP2, Keck Array and BICEP3 map through 2018 with Planck and WMAP data, the collaboration found no sign of primordial gravitational waves and limited their strength to a tensor-to-scalar ratio below 0.036 (95% confidence).
summary.technical: BK18: joint likelihood of BICEP2/Keck/BICEP3 (95/150/220 GHz, ~400-600 deg^2, depths 2.8, 2.8, 8.8 uK-arcmin) with WMAP and Planck maps vs lensed-LCDM + r + dust + synchrotron + noise; r_0.05 < 0.036 at 95% CL, sigma(r) = 0.009.

title: BICEP / Keck XIII: Improved Constraints on Primordial Gravitational Waves using Planck, WMAP, and BICEP/Keck Observations through the 2018 Observing Season
why_it_matters: The abstract calls these "the strongest constraints to date on primordial gravitational waves", which bound the energy scale of cosmic inflation.
